title: Entropy Production and Thermalization in Heavy-Quark Langevin Dynamics
abstract: Heavy quarks are often treated as Brownian probes of the quark-gluon plasma. We formulate the irreversible entropy balance of their momentum distribution and separate the production generated by collisions from the driving caused by an evolving medium. For linear dynamics the production splits into two positive contributions, from directed momentum and from the momentum width. A static bath obeys an exact H-theorem. A cooling bath adds an explicit driving term, and longitudinal Bjorken expansion enters as a separate kinematic drive rather than as collisional production. For a Bjorken temperature protocol we derive closed-form strong- and weak-coupling limits of the total production. At strong coupling it exceeds the initial relative entropy by a term linear in the relaxation time, whose quasistatic part has the thermodynamic-length form. At weak coupling it vanishes inversely with the relaxation time. A positive strong-coupling slope therefore guarantees maximal dissipation at intermediate coupling. The same structure holds for a relativistic Fokker-Planck equation with a Jüttner stationary state, solved numerically for charm and bottom quarks under the temperature protocol. Linear-response coefficients computed from the static generator reproduce both limits, and the numerical entropy balance is satisfied to high accuracy.
summary: This work investigates how heavy quarks thermalize in a cooling quark-gluon plasma by analyzing the irreversible entropy production. Using Langevin dynamics, the authors derive the entropy balance equation and find that the total entropy production peaks at intermediate coupling strengths. This provides crucial theoretical insights into the non-equilibrium transport properties of heavy quarks in QCD matter.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the irreversible entropy balance and thermalization process of heavy quarks moving through a cooling quark-gluon plasma (QGP).
main_result: The total entropy production exhibits a maximum at intermediate coupling strengths, and closed-form expressions for the production are derived for both strong and weak coupling limits.
method: The authors use the Langevin and Fokker-Planck formalisms to derive and analyze the entropy balance equation, separating production into distinct contributions.
model_or_system: The system models heavy quarks as Brownian probes interacting with a thermalizing, expanding QGP bath, analyzed using both nonrelativistic and relativistic descriptions.
key_observables: Entropy production rate ($\Pi$), Relative entropy ($KL[f||f_{eq}]$), Total entropy production ($\Sigma(t_f)$).
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($c_D$), Relaxation time ($	au$), Temperature protocol (Bjorken expansion).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the classical single-particle momentum density entropy and assumes a Markovian process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the static-bath entropy balance, the comparison of asymptotic limits (strong/weak coupling) to the exact solution for total entropy production, and the time evolution of entropy for charm and bottom quarks.
paper_structure: The paper develops from the general entropy balance formalism for a static bath to the driven case of a cooling QGP, deriving closed-form limits and numerically verifying the results for different heavy quark species.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of entropy balance principles to non-equilibrium transport in a hot, dense medium provides a strong theoretical framework applicable to open quantum systems far from equilibrium.
